haley: Heads-up from the int8 bring-up (lynx-int8). Not the usual array/truncation cases this time. We're seeing mixed-format streams: some responses contain an object followed by a newline and then an NDJSON line (object) in the same payload, e.g. a valid {"actions": [...]} followed by a separate line like {"log": "audit"}. Our funcall parser expects a single JSON object or a single top-level array and treats the extra NDJSON line as a parse error. Fail rate ~5/1000 in multibatch + kvcache=prefix.

omar: That's odd. Can you paste a sanitized raw capture? Trying to see if the model actually emits NDJSON or if assembler is concatenating two generations.

haley: Pasted sanitized snippet from the capture (raw bytes normalized):
```
{"actions": [{"tool":"create_ticket","params":{"title":"deploy"}}]}
{"meta": {"event":"audit","id":"a-923"}}
```
Note the two JSON documents separated by newline in a single stream. Baseline fp16 never did this. The NDJSON suffix sometimes appears only when we hit a cached prefix + batch>=6.

jules: Hypotheses: (1) model prompt/context shape with some retriever metadata is leaking into the generation tail under int8 quantization, (2) streaming assembler is concatenating a separate debug log fragment from the cache into the tail, or (3) a mirror/ensemble path is returning sidecar telemetry that the postproc is not stripping.

mirror-bot: mirror replay started: job_id mj-211, seeds=1200 model=lynx-int8 batch=8 capture=raw+token_ids. Artifacts: https://ci.internal/canary/mj-211 :satellite:

omar: Two quick probes: A) rerun same seeds with mirror disabled to rule out sidecar telemetry, B) rerun with kvcache=off to check assembly coupling, C) try a prompt anchor sentinel <ONLY_ACTIONS> and force the model to emit an explicit terminator. If A or B drops the phenomenon it's environmental rather than model.

haley: Ran A/B on a small sample: mirror=off => 1.1/1000; mirror=on => 4.9/1000. kvcache=off => 0.8/1000. So mirror+prefix seems to amplify it. Also observed that when NDJSON suffix is present, it often contains a tiny log-like object with keys like "meta" or "checkpoint".

jules: That leans infra-side. Likely we're accidentally stitching replica-side debug emissions into the response when we splice a cached prefix from a mirror. Could be a leftover trace print that ended up as tokens. Two mitigations: 1) quick sanitizer: if we see multiple top-level JSON docs separated by newline, keep only the first and tag as heuristic_strip_ndjson, 2) short-term: disable mirror telemetry splicing for int8 canaries, 3) long-term: instrument mirror nodes to avoid emitting sidecar tokens into the generation stream.

omar: I'll add a lightweight parser guard that treats an NDJSON suffix as truncation/sidecar and strips everything after the first closing '}' or ']' if the following non-whitespace starts with '{' on a new line. Count and alert on heuristic_strip_ndjson > 1/1000. Also add a small retry (single retry) so we can recover some legitimate cases.

haley: OK, gating that as emergency canary patch. Also please capture token ids for a couple of failing traces so we can decide whether tokens come from model or from a mirror-side print. If token ids point to printable ASCII for '{' and 'n' etc in a contiguous segment that suggests it's real token output, otherwise assembly duplication likely.

jules: Good plan. If it's mirror telemetry, we need to patch the mirror client to never return any debug/log tokens in the cache payload. Also let's add an A/B benchmark comparing structured-output F1 between fp16 and int8 on the same seed set to confirm there's no semantic quality regression when sanitized. If F1 drops materially after stripping NDJSON that would indicate model behavior change.

omar: Mirror token_id dumps attached to mj-211. Early look: tokens for suffix map to printable JSON characters and the suffix aligns with the cached-chunk splice point. Filing infra ticket linking artifacts. For now I'll land the sanitizer + single retry on canary and disable mirror telemetry in the offline mirroring path.

haley: Thanks. After the canary patch we reduced end-user parser errors by ~85% on the canary. Leaving the ticket open for infra to remove sidecar emissions and for the ML team to run the fp16 vs int8 structured-output benchmark on the sanitized traces. Post any raw captures here if you find non-retryable garbage. :sparkles:
